q-95527.name: Question 1
q-95527.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsech}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{x\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\operatorname{arsech}⁡(2x+1)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1))-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsech}⁡(2x+1)) \\  & =\frac{2}{2x+1}-(-\frac{1}{(2x+1)\sqrt{1-(2x+1)^{2}}})\cdot (2x+1)^{′} \\  & =\frac{2}{2x+1}+\frac{1}{(2x+1)\sqrt{1-4{x}^{2}-4x-1}}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{2}{2x+1}+\frac{2}{(2x+1)\sqrt{-4{x}^{2}-4x}} \\  & =\frac{2}{2x+1}(1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{-4x(x+1)}}) \\  & =\frac{2}{2x+1}(1+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{-x(x+1)}}).\end{aligned}
$$

q-95527.html:
Question 1
?

If y=ln⁡(2x+1)−arsech⁡(2x+1), then dydx=

a
22x+1(1+2−x(x+1))
b
22x+1+1−x(x+1)
c
22x+1(1+12−x(x+1))
d
22x+1(1−1−x(x+1))
e
22x+1−12−x(x+1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is ddx(arsech⁡x)=−1x1−x2.

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get dydx=ddx(ln⁡(2x+1)−arsech⁡(2x+1))=ddx(ln⁡(2x+1))−ddx(arsech⁡(2x+1))=22x+1−(−1(2x+1)1−(2x+1)2)⋅(2x+1)′=22x+1+1(2x+1)1−4x2−4x−1⋅2=22x+1+2(2x+1)−4x2−4x=22x+1(1+1−4x(x+1))=22x+1(1+12−x(x+1)).

q-95539.name: Question 2
q-95539.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cotangent function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2)+\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(x-1)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2))+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(x-1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{x-2}+\frac{1}{1-(x-1)^{2}}\cdot (x-1)^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{x-2}+\frac{1}{1-({x}^{2}-2x+1)}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{x-2}+\frac{1}{2x-{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{x-2}-\frac{1}{x(x-2)} \\  & =\frac{1}{x-2}(1-\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{x-1}{x(x-2)}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-95539.html:
Question 2
?

If y=ln⁡(x−2)+arcoth⁡(x−1), then dydx=

a
x(x−1)x−2
b
x+1x(x+2)
c
x(x−2)x−1
d
x−1x(x−2)
e
x+2x(x+1)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cotangent function is ddx(arcoth⁡x)=11−x2.

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

dydx=ddx(ln⁡(x−2)+arcoth⁡(x−1))=ddx(ln⁡(x−2))+ddx(arcoth⁡(x−1))=1x−2+11−(x−1)2⋅(x−1)′=1x−2+11−(x2−2x+1)⋅1=1x−2+12x−x2=1x−2−1x(x−2)=1x−2(1−1x)=x−1x(x−2).

q-341503.name: Question 3
q-341503.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsech}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{x\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{arsech}⁡({x}^{4})] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot [-\frac{1}{{x}^{4}\sqrt{1-{({x}^{4})}^{2}}}]\cdot {({x}^{4})}^{′} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4{x}^{4}\sqrt{1-{x}^{8}}}\cdot 4{x}^{3} \\  & =-\frac{1}{x\sqrt{1-{x}^{8}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-341553.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a product $u(x)\cdot v(x)$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x.$

Therefore, we apply the product rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & ={(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{arcsch}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot {(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x)}^{′} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{arcsch}⁡x\,+\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{arcsch}⁡x-\frac{1}{|x|}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-341558.name: Question 5
q-341558.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a product $u(x)\cdot v(x)$ with $u(x)=x+2$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x.$

Therefore, we apply the product rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & ={(x+2)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡x+(x+2)\cdot {(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)}^{′} \\  & =1\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡x\,+\,(x+2)\cdot (\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}) \\  & =\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x+\frac{x+2}{1-{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
